en: The Jātaka:
The Eighth Chapter,
the Section on Kaccāyana
4. The Sumaṅgala Jātaka:
“Having observed that one is greatly provoked to anger, a lord should not yet inflict punishment;”
It is improper and unfitting for one to violently incite sufferings upon another when it is not the right occasion; rather,
one should act from the knowledge that one possesses faith within oneself.
One should apply a penalty for another’s misconduct after personally considering,
“This is the purpose [of this case],” and then impose a punishment proportionate to it.
He does not burn others nor himself— he who,
uninfatuated, leads one from the wrong path to the right;
he who wields the rod as a lord in this world.
He who guards his speech does not fall from glory.
Those kṣatriyas who act without reflection,
being infatuated, mete out punishment impulsively.
Those joined with blame give up their lives;
even when liberated from this world, they go to a state of misery.
But those who delight in the Dhamma proclaimed by the Noble Ones—
Supreme are you in speech, mind, and deed;
established in peace, gentleness,
and concentration, such as you traverse both worlds.
I am a king, the lord of those who are like gods among men;
even if I should become angry, I restrain myself,
thus restraining the people of such a kind.
“I shall mete out punishment with wise compassion.
“O Kṣatriya, may both Śrī and Lakṣmī never forsake you, O lord of men!”
Free from anger, with a mind always serene and free from affliction,
may you, O Kshatriya endowed with these virtues, protect [the earth] for a hundred years.
One who abides by the noble conduct, is easy to speak to, and free from anger—
happy and free from oppression, he shall rule the earth;
and even after departing from here, he shall go to a happy destination.
Thus, by means of well-guided, well-spoken,
righteous, and methodical instruction,
one should extinguish the agitation of the great multitude.
“The great cloud [satisfied] the earth with water.
The fourth Jātaka, the Sumaṅgala Jātaka, is concluded.
